recommended_actions_freeform_experimenta: Immediately isolate the host dc01.corp.local from internal traffic to prevent further spread while preserving volatile memory for analysis.
Collect a full disk image, memory dump, and relevant system logs (Security Event Log, Sysmon, PowerShell transcripts) as soon as possible to preserve evidence of the lateral‑movement chain.

Run an in‑depth malware scan on all endpoints that have communicated with dc01.corp.local during the time window surrounding the logon event, focusing on executables and scripts that may have been dropped or executed remotely.

Cross‑reference the 42 correlated events against known attack patterns (e.g., Pass‑the‑Hash, credential dumping tools) to identify any common artifacts such as hash values, file paths, or registry modifications.
Perform a network traffic audit for outbound connections originating from dc01.corp.local after the logon to detect potential data exfiltration or command‑and‑control activity.
Engage threat intelligence feeds to see if the external IP 100.72.44.19 has been previously associated with malicious actors, even though no provider information is currently available.
If feasible, conduct a live‑response session on dc01.corp.local to capture any active processes or scheduled tasks that may be part of an ongoing compromise.
Document all findings in a chain‑of‑custody log and prepare a preliminary incident report for the SOC team to review and decide on containment versus eradication strategies.
triage_rationale_experimental: The event shows a valid account logging in from an unknown external IP with many lateral‑movement indicators, but the lack of provider data and absence of confirmed malicious payloads leave enough ambiguity to warrant further investigation before labeling it definitively as a true positive.
